transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, well, I came in because... lately, I've been having a really hard time. I recently tried to take my art and turn it into a real freelance business, you know, to make some money from it. But ever since I started doing that, I just... I keep getting really wound up over everything. Like, dealing with invoices and client messages just stresses me out so much. So I end up avoiding them entirely. And then, before I know it, I'm just sitting at my kitchen table crying, or I'm forgetting to do normal, everyday things, like paying my own bills. It's just gotten to be too much.
Do you find that you feel this way about almost everything in your life, or is this feeling of being overwhelmed strictly tied to your new freelance business?

Um, no, it's really just tied to the freelance stuff. Before I tried to turn my art into a business, I didn't feel like this at all. I was perfectly fine handling my normal day-to-day life. It's just... ever since I added the business side of things, that specific part is what makes me so overwhelmed, and then it kind of spills over into me forgetting my regular chores. But the stress itself is definitely coming from the business.
Beyond the feelings of being overwhelmed and stressed, have you been experiencing a persistent low mood, sadness, or a loss of interest in things you usually enjoy?

Not really, no. I mean, I get upset and cry when the business stuff piles up, but I wouldn't say I feel sad all the time. It's not a constant low mood or anything like that. And I still like the things I usually enjoy. Like, I still love making art when it's just for fun, and I haven't lost interest in my hobbies. I'm just... really stressed out by the business side of it.
When you feel overwhelmed by the business tasks, do you find yourself acting out in ways that are disruptive, such as being reckless, getting into arguments, or violating the rights of others?

Um, no, not at all. I don't get into arguments or act reckless or anything like that. When the stress hits, I just sort of... shut down, I guess. Like I said, I just avoid my emails and end up crying by myself. I definitely don't lash out at anyone else or do anything disruptive.
When you feel this overwhelming stress, do you experience physical sensations like a racing heart, trembling, or feeling keyed up or on edge?

Um, no, not really. I don't get a racing heart or start shaking or anything. It doesn't really feel like a physical panic. Like I was saying, I just sort of shut down and cry when it's all too much. But I don't feel physically keyed up or on edge, it's just... more of a mental block, I guess.
Even though you don't feel physically keyed up, do you find yourself feeling nervous, worried, or anxious about the business tasks?

No, I wouldn't say I feel nervous or... or anxious about it. It's not like I sit around worrying about what's going to happen or anything. It's really just that when I actually have to sit down and do those tasks, or when I look at all the emails, I just feel completely overwhelmed by the sheer amount of it. But I don't have that anxious, worried feeling leading up to it.
When you are in one of these periods where you feel overwhelmed and shut down, do you find that you also feel a sense of hopelessness or worthlessness?

No, I wouldn't say I feel hopeless or worthless. It's really just the stress of the tasks themselves. I don't feel bad about myself as a person, and I don't feel like things are never going to get better. It's just... in that moment, the amount of work is too much, and I just can't deal with it. But it doesn't turn into feeling worthless.
When you are feeling overwhelmed, do you find that you have trouble focusing, or do you feel like your mind goes blank, which makes it even harder to get your work done?

No, I don't really have trouble focusing, and my mind doesn't go blank. I know exactly what needs to be done, and I understand the emails just fine when I read them. It's really just the sheer volume of it all that makes me shut down. So it's not an issue with my focus... I just get overwhelmed by how much there is to get through and feel like I can't do it right then.
When you find yourself crying because of the overwhelming volume of work, do you feel a sense of intense sadness or despair in those moments, even if it is brief?

No, I wouldn't call it intense sadness or despair. It's not like I'm crying because I'm heartbroken or anything like that. It's more just... frustration, I guess? It's just the stress bubbling over because there's so much to do and I just want it to be done. So it's not a deep sadness, it's just the overwhelming feeling of it all coming out.
When you are feeling this way, do you find yourself feeling any lack of energy, or perhaps feeling like you are moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

No, I don't think so. I don't feel drained of energy or anything, and I don't feel like I'm moving in slow motion. I just... I just walk away from the computer or put my head down for a minute. My energy level is normal, it's just that I'm avoiding the tasks.
When you feel overwhelmed by these tasks, do you find yourself experiencing persistent feelings of apprehension, tension, or a sense of dread?

No, I wouldn't say I feel dread or anything like that. I don't feel tense or on edge all the time. It really is just when I look at the pile of things I have to do, I just feel like I can't handle it in that moment. But I don't walk around feeling scared or worried about it constantly. It's just a reaction to seeing how much there is.
When you feel overwhelmed by these tasks, do you find yourself doing things that are out of character for you, such as acting in a way that is defiant, rebellious, or breaking rules?

No, definitely not. I'm not acting out or breaking any rules. I'm just... I'm just avoiding the work, really. I might put it off or ignore it for a bit, but I'm not doing anything rebellious or out of character like that.
When you are feeling overwhelmed and you cry, do you experience a noticeable feeling of being down, blue, or discouraged during those moments?

No, I don't think I feel down or blue, really. I mean, I cry because it's just too much at once, but it's not like a deep sadness or feeling discouraged about life in general. It's just the stress of the moment spilling over, I guess. Once I step away for a bit, that feeling passes.
When you are in the middle of these moments of feeling overwhelmed, do you feel any internal sense of agitation, nervousness, or restlessness?

No, not really. I don't feel nervous or restless. It's not an agitated feeling, it's just... I just feel overwhelmed by the sheer amount of things I need to do. I don't get jittery or anything like that.
When you are in these moments of feeling overwhelmed, do you notice yourself becoming more irritable or easily annoyed with people or things around you?

No, I wouldn't say I get irritable or annoyed with other people. It's really just about the tasks themselves. I don't take it out on anyone around me, I just... I just feel like I can't handle the workload in that moment. But I'm not snapping at people or getting frustrated with things like that.
